Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsHarry Brook's record ODI double ton in vain as Sri Lanka pull off epic chaseIn one lineHarry Brook's record-breaking ODI double century was in vain as Sri Lanka pulled off an epic run chase to win.Key highlights• Brook's Record-Breaking InningsEngland captain Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in ODI history, making 202 off 116 balls and becoming the first Englishman to score 200 in the format.• Sri Lanka's Epic Run ChaseSri Lanka successfully chased down England's mammoth total of 429 for four, sealing a two-wicket win with one ball to spare in the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.• Standout Batting PerformancesPavan Rathnayake top-scored for Sri Lanka with 130 runs, while teammates Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both narrowly missed out on centuries with 97 runs each.• Tournament Standings ImpactThe defeat leaves England at the bottom of the tri-series standings after losing both their opening matches, requiring wins in their remaining games to reach the final.Key statistics202Brook's record double-century score429 for fourEngland's innings total130Pavan Rathnayake's top score for Sri Lanka435Record for highest ODI chase set by South Africa2006Year South Africa set the highest ODI chase recordProcessed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.The England captain hit the fastest-ever ODI double hundred, making 202 off 116 balls to propel his team to a mammoth 429 for four after they were put in to bat.Batters thoroughly dominated in Rawalpindi as Brook also hit the first ODI double century by an England player. However, Sri Lanka proved up to the challenge as Pavan Rathnayake scored 130, with Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both making 97.South Africa hold the record for the highest ODI chase, knocking off a target of 435 against Australia at Johannesburg in 2006.Brook became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format, but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win with one ball to spare.ICC Test Rankings | Brook reclaims top spot, Bumrah stays as No.1 bowlerThe 27-year-old rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India's Shubman Gill.In the process, Brook also eclipsed England's highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes.ICC rankings | Iyer rises to career-best 7th in T20Is; Gill consolidates numero uno position in ODIsBrook's scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England's innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage.He made 202 from 116 deliveries, peppering the Sri Lanka attack with 21 fours and 10 sixes before departing to warm applause from the crowd.The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore.Joe Root provided strong support with 69 off 66 balls.But the total proved insufficient as Sri Lanka completed the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.Pavan Rathnayake top-scored with 130 from 106 deliveries, while opener Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both fell three runs short of centuries.Needing six runs from the final two deliveries, Sri Lanka sealed victory when Liyanage launched Josh Tongue over long-off for six, leaving Brook's record-breaking innings all in vain.Tongue was England's most successful bowler with 3-79.England lost by 87 runs at the same venue in Rawalpindi to Pakistan, who lead the table with two wins from two.Pakistan, who beat Sri Lanka and England in their two games, will face England in Lahore on Sunday in the next match in the tri-series.

brief_bullets: England captain Harry Brook made history by smashing the fastest double-century in One-day International (ODI) history, scoring 202 off 116 balls against Sri Lanka in a tri-series match at Rawalpindi. His record-breaking innings, the first ODI double ton by an Englishman, propelled England to a mammoth 429 for four. However, Sri Lanka mounted an extraordinary chase, with Pavan Rathnayake scoring 130 and Avishka Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both adding 97, ultimately securing a two-wicket victory with one ball to spare. This epic pursuit marks the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history, leaving England at the bottom of the tournament standings after two defeats.
why_it_matters_bullets: This historic match highlights cricket's evolving high-scoring dynamics and significantly impacts England's tri-series progression.

brief_bullets: At a United Nations interactive dialogue, India’s First Secretary Bhavika Mangalanandan sharply rebuked Pakistan for its hypocrisy regarding religious freedom and funeral rights. Responding to a UN report criticizing India’s security operations in Jammu and Kashmir, Mangalanandan highlighted that Pakistan famously refused to claim its own soldiers killed during the 1999 Kargil War, forcing the Indian Army to provide them with dignified Islamic burials. She further dismissed the UN rapporteur’s findings as unsupported, arguing that Pakistan lacks the moral standing to lecture India on human rights while its own minorities face systemic abuse. India maintains that sovereign states must retain the legal authority to restrict funeral rites for terrorists who violate the fundamental right to life.
why_it_matters_bullets: This diplomatic confrontation underscores India's aggressive strategy to delegitimize Pakistan's international advocacy by exposing its historical and domestic contradictions.
